dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: صباح الخير يا يوسف.
dialogue.english: Good morning, Youssef.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: صباح النور، لاباس؟
dialogue.english: Good morning, are you well?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله، لاباس. شحال فالساعة دابا؟
dialogue.english: Thank God, fine. What time is it now?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: باقي نعسانة، فقت بكري اليوم.
dialogue.english: I'm still sleepy, I woke up early today.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: وأنا بغيت قهوة قبل كلشي.
dialogue.english: And I want coffee first thing.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: أنا بحالك. غسلت وجهي ولبست حوايجي بسرعة.
dialogue.transliteration: ana b7aalek. ghsselt wejhi w-lbest 7waayji bsor3a.
dialogue.english: Same as you. I washed my face and got dressed quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: وغسلتي سنانك؟
dialogue.english: And did you brush your teeth?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: إيه طبعا. واش غادي تخرج للخدمة دابا؟
dialogue.transliteration: ee tab3an. waash ghaadi tkhrej l-khedma daba?
dialogue.english: Yes of course. Are you leaving for work now?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: إيه، ولكن كاين برد بزاف فالصباح.
dialogue.transliteration: ee, walakin kayn bard bzzaf f-ssba7.
dialogue.english: Yes, but it's very cold in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: يالله، ماتفوتش الطوبيس.
dialogue.english: Come on, don't miss the bus.

lessons.culture: In Morocco a morning greeting is "sba7 l-kheer" answered "sba7 n-noor", usually followed by "laabas?", and it is normal to add "l-7amdulillah" in the reply. Most people start the day with tea or coffee and bread, often before leaving the house.

exercises.prompt: Someone says to you: "صباح الخير". Reply naturally.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: The fixed everyday reply to "صباح الخير" is "صباح النور".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "لاباس؟". Reply naturally.

too_formal.item: أنا بخير والحمد لله، شكرا على سؤالك
too_formal.feedback: Correct but far more elaborate than the quick everyday reply.

exercises.tip: "لاباس" is asked and answered with the same word, plus "الحمد لله".

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "بغيت _____ قبل كلشي." English meaning: I want coffee first thing.

too_formal.feedback: This wording is more explicit and formal than the simple everyday word.

exercises.tip: "قبل كلشي" means before anything else.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: "هادي _____." English meaning: It's seven o'clock.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: Darija says the hour as a plain number with the article: "السبعة".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Darija: "I woke up early."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "فقت" is the everyday Darija verb for "woke up".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Darija: "I left for work."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "خدمة" is the everyday Darija word for work.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Darija: "I missed the bus."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "طوبيس" is the everyday word for bus, and "فاتني" means "it passed me by".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I brushed my teeth"?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: Darija says "washed" for teeth as well as for the face.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Early morning is very cold"?

too_formal.item: الجو بارد جدا في الصباح الباكر
too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "كاين" here means "there is".

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "بكري / للخدمة / خرجت"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: Verb, then place, then time is the natural spoken order here.

phrases.arabic: خاصني نكمل هاد الخدمة قبل الظهر

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: وصلت للخدمة. شنو كاين اليوم؟
dialogue.english: I arrived at work. What's on today?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: عندي ريونيون فالعاشرة.
dialogue.english: I have a meeting at ten.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: والو، ولكن عندي خدمة بزاف دابا.
dialogue.english: Nothing, but I have a lot of work now.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: وأنا خاصني نكمل هاد الخدمة قبل الظهر.
dialogue.transliteration: w-ana khaassni nkemmel haad l-khedma 9bel ddohr.
dialogue.english: And I have to finish this task before noon.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: أنا جيعانة، بغيت ناكل شي حاجة.
dialogue.english: I'm hungry, I want to eat something.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: فين كاتتغدى نتي؟
dialogue.english: Where do you have lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: كانتغدى فالخدمة.
dialogue.english: I have lunch at work.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: تعبت شوية دابا. كانقلب على الستيلو ديالي وما لقيتوش.
dialogue.transliteration: t3ebt shwiya daba. kan9elleb 3la stilo dyaali w-ma l9itoosh.
dialogue.english: I'm a bit tired now. I'm looking for my pen and I can't find it.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: هاهو فوق الطابلة. غادي نعيط ليك العشية.
dialogue.transliteration: haahwa foo9 ttabla. ghaadi n3ayyet lik l-3eshiya.
dialogue.english: Here it is on the table. I'll call you in the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: شكرا. نتلاقاو بعد الريونيون.
dialogue.english: Thanks. See you after the meeting.

pair.english: Do you have a meeting today?

lessons.culture: In Moroccan workplaces lunch is usually taken between twelve and two, and colleagues say "bismillah" before eating. Someone who sees you eating may say "b-ssa7a w-raa7a", wishing you health and ease.

exercises.prompt: A colleague asks you: "فين كاتتغدى؟". Reply naturally.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "كاتتغدى" is "you have lunch", "كانتغدى" is "I have lunch".

exercises.tip: "ريونيون" is the everyday word for a meeting, and "ف" joins with "العاشرة".

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "خاصني" means "I must", and the verb follows directly.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Darija: "I arrived at work."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "للخدمة" is "to work", the two words are joined.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Darija: "I have a lot of work now."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "بزاف" is "a lot" and "دابا" is "now".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Darija: "I finished my work early today."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "ساليت" is the everyday word for "I finished".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I'm looking for my pen"?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "ستيلو" is the everyday word for a pen.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I'll call you in the afternoon"?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "نعيط" means "I call" and "غادي" makes it future.

exercises.prompt: Put these segments in a natural order: "قبل الظهر / نكمل / خاصني / هاد الخدمة"
exercises.answer: خاصني نكمل هاد الخدمة قبل الظهر
accepted: خاصني نكمل هاد الخدمة قبل الظهر
خاصني نكمل هاد الخدمة قبل الضهر

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "خاصني" comes first, then the verb, then the object, then the time.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: مساء الخير، رجعتي للدار؟
dialogue.english: Good evening, you came back home?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: مساء النور، إيه رجعت للدار. تعبت بزاف اليوم.
dialogue.transliteration: msaa n-noor, ee rj3et l-daar. t3ebt bzzaf lyoum.
dialogue.english: Good evening, yes I came back home. I got very tired today.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: ما عرفتش، غير بغيت ندوش الأول.
dialogue.english: I don't know, I just want to shower first.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: مزيان. وبعد واش نشوفو شي مسلسل؟
dialogue.transliteration: mzyaan. w-ba3d waash nshoufo shi msalsal?
dialogue.english: Fine. And after, shall we watch a series?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: الجو زوين فالمسا، يالله نخرجو نتمشاو شوية.
dialogue.transliteration: ljaw zwiin f-lmsa, yaallah nkhorjo ntmeshaw shwiya.
dialogue.english: The weather is nice in the evening, let's go out for a little walk.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: مزيان، ولكن بغيت نعيط لعائلتي الأول.
dialogue.transliteration: mzyaan, walakin bghit n3ayyet l-3aa2ilti l-lawwal.
dialogue.english: Fine, but I want to call my family first.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: عادي. أنا شفت صحابي فالمسا وضحكنا بزاف.
dialogue.transliteration: 3aadi. ana shft s7aabi f-lmsa w-d7ekna bzzaf.
dialogue.english: No problem. I saw my friends in the evening and we laughed a lot.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: غادي نرقد بكري الليلة، باقي نعسانة.
dialogue.transliteration: ghaadi nreqed bekri llila, ba9i n3saana.
dialogue.english: I'll sleep early tonight, I'm still sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: وأنا بحالك. تصبح على خير.
dialogue.english: Same for me. Good night.

pair.english: What will we eat for dinner?
Do we want to watch a series?

lessons.culture: Moroccan families usually eat dinner around eight or nine, and in warm weather many people go out for a stroll or to a cafe afterwards. "tsba7 3la kheer" is answered "w-nta men ahlo", and the same reply works for a woman with "w-nti men ahlo".

exercises.tip: The fixed everyday reply to "مساء الخير" is "مساء النور".

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "من أهله" means "you too are among the people of good".

exercises.tip: "الليلة" means tonight, and "رقد" is the everyday verb for sleeping.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "صحابي" is the everyday word for "my friends".

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "يالله" starts a suggestion like "come on, let's".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "The weather is nice in the evening"?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "زوين" is the everyday word for nice or beautiful.

phrases.arabic: لْحَد، التّنِين، التّلَات، لَرْبْعَا، لْخْمِيس، الْجُمْعَة، الْسّبْت
phrases.transliteration: l7ed, ttnin, ttlaata, larba3, lkhmiis, jjem3a, ssbt

phrases.arabic: السّيمَانَة الْجَايَة عِنْدَنَا رِيونْيون نَهَار التّلَات
عِنْدِي الخِدْمَة كُل نَهَار إِلّا الْجُمْعَة وَالْسّبْت
phrases.transliteration: 3ndi l-khedma kol nhaar illa jjem3a w-ssbt

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: اليوم لحد، وغدا التنين.
dialogue.english: Today is Sunday, and tomorrow is Monday.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: إيه، الويكاند كايدوز بسرعة.
dialogue.english: Yes, the weekend passes quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: السيمانة الجاية عندنا ريونيون نهار التلات.
dialogue.english: Next week we have a meeting on Tuesday.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: مزيان. نهار لربعا كانخدم حتى للمسا.
dialogue.english: Fine. On Wednesday I work until the evening.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: وأنا عندي الخدمة كل نهار إلا الجمعة والسبت.
dialogue.transliteration: w-ana 3ndi l-khedma kol nhaar illa jjem3a w-ssbt.
dialogue.english: And I have work every day except Friday and Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: نهار لخميس كانشوف صحابي.
dialogue.english: On Thursday I see my friends.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: الجمعة نهار الصلاة والراحة، غادي نمشي للجامع.
dialogue.transliteration: jjem3a nhaar ssalaa w-rraa7a, ghaadi nmshi l-jaam3.
dialogue.english: Friday is the day of prayer and rest, I'll go to the mosque.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: أش ناوي تدير فالويكاند الجاي؟
dialogue.english: What do you plan to do on the coming weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: زوين، ونتلاقاو نهار لخميس.
dialogue.english: Nice, and we'll meet on Thursday.

pair.english: What do you plan to do on the weekend?

lessons.culture: In Morocco most offices work Monday to Friday, with a longer midday break on Friday for the congregational prayer, so "except Friday and Saturday" fits only some workers, such as shopkeepers and cafe staff who take their own days off. Many families eat couscous after Friday prayer, and "nhaar" (day) is often placed before the day name.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "فوقاش الريونيون؟". Say it is on Tuesday at ten.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "فوقاش" means "when" and is answered with "نهار" plus the day.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "كانمشيو" is "we go", the present habit.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "نهار" plus the day name means "on that day".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Darija: "Tomorrow is Monday."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "غدا" is "tomorrow", and "التنين" is the spoken form of Monday.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Darija: "On Wednesday I work until the evening."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "كانخدم" is "I work" and "حتى" is "until".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Darija: "The weekend comes quickly."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "الويكاند" is the everyday word for the weekend.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Friday is the day of prayer and rest"?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "نهار" is the everyday word for "day".

exercises.prompt: Which question means "When is the meeting?"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "فوقاش" means "when".

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: The day comes first, then the verb, then the place.

reply.english: I read and go out with my friends.

phrases.transliteration: lbaare7 Tayyebt l3sha l l3aa2ila dyaali

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.arabic: بصح؟ شحال كتقرا؟
dialogue.english: Really? How much do you read?

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.arabic: ما شاء الله! أنا ما كنقراش بزاف.
dialogue.transliteration: maa shaa2 llaah! ana ma kan9raash bzzaaf.
dialogue.english: Masha Allah! I don't read much.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: مزيان! شنو كطيب؟
dialogue.english: Nice! What do you cook?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: شنو طيبتي؟
dialogue.english: What did you cook?

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.arabic: طاجين بالدجاج والزيتون. وانتا، واش كتبغي الخط العربي؟
dialogue.transliteration: Taajeen b ddjaaj w zzeetoon. w nta, waash katbghi lkhaTT l3arabi?
dialogue.english: A chicken and olive tagine. And you, do you like Arabic calligraphy?

dialogue.speaker: Hamza
dialogue.arabic: يالاه نمشيو لمعرض الخط فالمدينة القديمة.
dialogue.transliteration: yallaah nmshiw l ma3raD lkhaTT f lmdeena l9deema.
dialogue.english: Let's go to the calligraphy exhibition in the old medina.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: واخا، يالاه!
dialogue.english: Okay, let's go!

pair.english: What do you do in your free time?

response.english: I read and go out with my friends.

pair.english: Do you have time this evening?

lessons.culture: Free time in Casablanca and Rabat is often spent in a cafe with friends, walking on the seafront in the evening, or with family at the weekend. Morocco has its own style of Arabic handwriting, the Maghribi script, and many young people go hiking in the Atlas mountains in spring.

exercises.prompt: Your friend asks: "آش كدير فوقت الفراغ؟" Say you read and go out with your friends.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "كن" in front of a verb means I do it as a habit.

exercises.prompt: Your friend asks: "واش عندك الوقت هاد العشية؟" Say no, you don't have time.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: Darija wraps "not" around the word: "ما ... ش".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "الهواية ديالي هي _____." Meaning: My hobby is reading.

too_formal.feedback: "المطالعة" is the school word; in speech reading is "القراية".

exercises.tip: "قرا" is to read and "القراية" is reading, also studying.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "الوقت كيدوز _____ ملي كنقرا." Meaning: Time passes quickly when I read.

too_formal.feedback: "بسرعة" is understood, but "بالزربة" is the everyday Darija.

exercises.tip: "زرب" is to hurry.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I like cooking."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "طيب" is to cook; "الطيابة" is cooking.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I grow flowers in the garden."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: Flowers are "النوار"; a garden is "جنان" or "جردة".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I spend my time with my family."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "دوز" is to spend (time), from "داز", to pass.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I climb mountains with my friends"?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct Modern Standard Arabic, not how it is said in Darija.

exercises.tip: "طلع" is to go up, to climb.

exercises.prompt: Which word means "week" in Darija?

too_formal.feedback: "أسبوع" is MSA; Darija uses "سيمانة" from French semaine.

exercises.tip: Every week is "كل سيمانة".

lessons.culture: Football is the great passion: in Casablanca nearly everyone is either for Wydad or for Raja, and their derby stops the city. Horse riding has deep roots in Morocco through the tbourida, the traditional display of riders firing powder together, and in the evening many people walk or jog along the seafront.

exercises.tip: Football is simply "الكورة", the ball.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says: "نتمشاو مع بعضياتنا من بعد الصلاة؟" Say okay, after the afternoon prayer.

challenge.title: Plan Your Week in Darija
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short conversation about a day and the week ahead, at least 10 lines. It must include a morning greeting and its reply, a question about the time, a statement about being tired or sleepy, an evening greeting and its reply, the good-night exchange, a question about when a meeting is, and a plan for the weekend. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 7.
required_elements: A morning greeting using صباح الخير and its reply صباح النور.
A statement about waking up or being sleepy, using فقت بكري or باقي نعسان.
A question using شحال فالساعة دابا؟ and a time answer.
A statement about being tired or having a lot of work, using تعبت or عندي خدمة بزاف.
An evening greeting using مساء الخير and its reply مساء النور.
The good-night exchange using تصبح على خير and وانت من أهله.
A question using فوقاش؟ and its answer.
A statement naming at least two days of the week.
A plan for the weekend using الويكاند.
At least one invitation or suggestion, such as واش بغيتي تجي معانا؟ or يالله نخرجو.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: صباح الخير، لاباس عليك اليوم؟
dialogue.english: Good morning, how are you today?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: صباح النور، الحمد لله، ولكن باقي نعسان شوية.
dialogue.transliteration: sba7 n-noor, l-7amdulillah, walakin ba9i n3saan shwiya.
dialogue.english: Good morning, thank God, but I'm still a bit sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: شحال فالساعة دابا؟
dialogue.english: What time is it now?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: هادي السبعة، خاصني نخرج للخدمة.
dialogue.english: It's seven, I have to leave for work.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: أنا عندي خدمة بزاف هاد السيمانة.
dialogue.english: I have a lot of work this week.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: فوقاش الريونيون ديالنا؟
dialogue.english: When is our meeting?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: نهار التلات فالعاشرة، ونهار لخميس كانشوف صحابي.
dialogue.transliteration: nhaar ttlaata f-l3aashra, w-nhaar lkhmiis kanshoof s7aabi.
dialogue.english: On Tuesday at ten, and on Thursday I see my friends.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: مساء الخير، رجعت للدار وتعبت بزاف اليوم.
dialogue.transliteration: msaa l-kheer, rj3et l-daar w-t3ebt bzzaf lyoum.
dialogue.english: Good evening, I came back home and I got very tired today.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: مساء النور. أش ناوي تدير فالويكاند؟
dialogue.transliteration: msaa n-noor. ash naawi tdiir f-lwikaand?
dialogue.english: Good evening. What do you plan to do on the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: نهار السبت كانمشيو للسوق. واش بغيتي تجي معانا؟
dialogue.transliteration: nhaar ssbt kanmshiw l-ssoo9. waash bghiti tji m3aana?
dialogue.english: On Saturday we go to the market. Do you want to come with us?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: إيه، يالله. غادي نرقد بكري الليلة، تصبح على خير.
dialogue.transliteration: ee, yaallah. ghaadi nreqed bekri llila, tsba7 3la kheer.
dialogue.english: Yes, come on. I'll sleep early tonight, good night.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: وانت من أهله.
dialogue.english: And you too.
